title: Practice: Reaction Rates and Energy
description: Low-stakes practice on factors affecting reaction rate and exothermic versus endothermic reactions.

questions.question: Which statement best defines reaction rate?
options: How fast reactants are converted into products
How heavy the products are after a reaction
How colorful the reactants are before mixing
How many atoms are shown in a formula
questions.explanation: Reaction rate describes the speed of a reaction, or how quickly reactants change into products.

questions.question: Why does refrigeration help preserve food?
options: It increases the concentration of food particles
It lowers temperature and slows many spoilage reactions
It turns all bacteria into catalysts
It removes all oxygen from the food
questions.explanation: Lower temperature slows particle motion and reduces the rate of many chemical and microbial spoilage processes.

questions.question: True or False: Crushing a solid into powder usually increases its reaction rate because more surface area is exposed.
questions.explanation: True. Powder exposes more solid surface to the other reactant, allowing more collisions at the same time.

questions.question: A catalyst is best described as a substance that:
options: slows every reaction by lowering temperature
speeds up a reaction without being used up overall
is always the main product of the reaction
changes a chemical reaction into a physical change
questions.explanation: A catalyst increases reaction rate and is not consumed overall, so it can continue helping the reaction.

questions.question: A reaction that releases energy to the surroundings is called ____.
questions.explanation: Exothermic reactions release energy, often making the surroundings warmer.

questions.question: True or False: Increasing reactant concentration usually increases reaction rate because there are more reacting particles in the same volume.
questions.explanation: True. More particles in the same space usually means more collisions per second.

questions.question: An instant cold pack becomes cold when activated. Which energy description best fits?
options: Exothermic, because energy leaves the surroundings
Endothermic, because energy is absorbed from the surroundings
Catalytic, because no energy is involved
questions.explanation: A cold pack absorbs energy from its surroundings, so the surroundings feel cooler. That is endothermic behavior.

questions.question: Explain why sawdust or thin wood shavings can catch fire more easily than a thick log.
questions.correctAnswer: Sawdust or thin shavings have much greater surface area exposed to oxygen, so combustion can happen faster than in a thick log.
questions.explanation: Greater surface area allows more fuel particles to contact oxygen at once, increasing the rate of combustion.
